G1.name: Protocol correctness
G1.description: All valid/invalid RPC, MMIO, AXI4-Lite, and AXI4-Stream contracts behave as specified.

G2.name: Transaction integrity
G2.description: Every accepted request is traceable 1-to-1 to its RTL response and m3_transactions.jsonl record.

G3.name: Cycle correctness
G3.description: Bridge cycle counts agree with direct Verilator Vaa_qec_top clock progression (C_latency = C_completed - C_accepted).

G4.name: Functional equivalence
G4.description: Bridge-mediated RTL matches standalone Vaa_qec_top across all 256 (sx, sz) syndromes, inhomogeneous wx != wz, K=1..5, and osd_mode=0..2.

G5.name: Lockstep correctness
G5.description: QEMU ARM Cortex-A9 (32-bit) and ARM64 Cortex-A53 (64-bit) guest transactions reconcile deterministically with bridge and Verilator RTL.

G6.name: Epoch correctness
G6.description: Software HAL and RTL agree on shadow/active triple-buffered weight banks, shadow_locked_c SLVERR protection, epoch_count, and epoch_irq.

G7.name: Fault recovery
G7.description: Injected RPC, socket, bridge, RTL, and guest faults recover safely without blind retry of non-idempotent SYNDROME_TRANSFER or COMMIT.

G8.name: Reproducibility & fidelity disclosure
G8.description: Deterministic replay, per-line durable m3_transactions.jsonl, SHA-256 provenance manifests, and explicit co-simulation boundary disclosures.

fidelity_disclaimers.qemu_scope: QEMU execution uses Linux user-mode instruction/ABI translation (qemu-arm -cpu cortex-a9 and qemu-aarch64 -cpu cortex-a53) forwarding AF_UNIX socket syscalls to the host kernel. It validates 32-bit/64-bit ARM ELF ABI, struct packing, endianness, Q7.8 serialization, and RPC lockstep, but does NOT emulate a full-system kernel, device tree, physical /dev/mem AXI bus, or GIC hardware interrupt controller.
fidelity_disclaimers.rtl_timing_scope: Verilator cycle counts prove cycle-exact synchronous RTL state-machine behavior of aa_qec_top at a nominal 4.0 ns (250 MHz) simulation period, but do NOT substitute for post-place-and-route Vivado Static Timing Analysis (WNS/TNS), physical clock-domain crossing jitter, or cryogenic/analog readout physics.
